title: Verify managed speech configuration at the child process boundary
summary: Forward explicit non-secret configuration narrowly and test what the real child receives; validate healthy lock diagnostics with an ENOENT-preserving fixture.
reusable_steps: Forward explicit non-secret configuration narrowly and test what the real child receives; validate healthy lock diagnostics with an ENOENT-preserving fixture
expected_outcome:
When a managed backend replaces a direct command, audit every configuration value consumed by its child. Forward only the named model directory/name, device, compute type and language settings through safeExecResult overrides. Keep the shared environment policy unchanged and preserve request-level precedence. Execute the production Python bridge against a hermetic fake model to verify actual child configuration, Unicode, defaults and exclusion of a non-allowlisted credential; a mocked spawn call alone cannot establish that boundary. This verifies configuration plumbing, not GPU execution, speech accuracy or native Windows behavior.

Test diagnostic APIs according to their contract: a free or verifiably owned lock has no recovery diagnostic. Use an IO fixture that preserves ENOENT for missing cleanup guards, and keep real-I/O acquisition, contention, owner record, release and reacquisition coverage. A wrapped missing-file error can falsely pass an assertion about a live owner. Do not redesign the lock protocol to fix a test.

A filename in a prefix-based permission policy is not inherently an exact-file grant. Revoke one-time authoring grants after the requested artifact exists, verify descendants and neighboring paths are denied, and avoid shipping broader continuing authority.
